items.content:
It has taken me two months to see that these are the same idea.

If meaning lives in the gap between shots and not in the shots
themselves, then horror does not need a monster. It needs two innocuous
images and the right interval. **The audience builds the monster.** They
always did — every effect I have ever admired was a collaboration I
mistook for craftsmanship.

Which means you could make something frightening out of entirely ordinary
footage. A door. A hand. A road. In the right order.

I want to try this.

summary: Two months on: the audience builds the monster from the gap
title: Kuleshov, again, and what it implies about horror
